title: Formats the player can deliver
statement: Use a question format only once the student's own player has been seen to render it, and keep a fallback format for the rest.
example: Three item types uploaded without an error and then showed students an empty quiz.
detail: Live probes of the reading project's delivery platform found that matching, hot-text and text-entry items uploaded cleanly (201, valid QTI, GET 200) but showed an empty quiz to students and had to be turned into single-choice items (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0009-timeback-alpha-read-packager.qmd`). A production reading course there held 1,077 items, 100% single-choice, with no interactive item ever rendered, while the project's Grade 5 contract required all six formats, so it could fully certify a form that could not be delivered; the action was a delivery gate asking for a live render in the student's view of every non-choice format, with a choice-only fallback form (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0072-learnings-from-incept-map-proxy-2026-06-25.qmd`). A publishing plugin distilled from AP science builds exists to stop items that return 200 OK but render broken or empty in the student's view (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0020-incept-timeback-plugin.qmd`).
against: The project chose not to cut its courses down to single choice for the platform's sake: all-choice is a fallback only, and a separate delivery app was planned for the richer formats (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0022-incept-team-sync-2026-06-17.qmd`).
